pg. 3                                    James C. Reed Irrevocable Trust - James Reed Direct Testimony
                                      I. INTRODUCTION

Q. Please state your name and address.

A. My name is James C. Reed. My mailing address is RO. Box 732, Fairfield, Texas 75840.


Q. Please explain why you are providing testimony in this docket.

A. I am an owner of property located in San Saba County that is directly affected by

proposed Route Vl. My ranch is a wildlife restoration property, and the proposed

transmission line will negatively affect ongoing efforts to restore and protect dwindling

wildlife species on the property.


Q. Have you previously provided testimony before the Public Utility Commission of

Texas?

A. No, I have not previously provided testimony before the Commission.


Q. What route do you oppose?

A. I oppose proposed Route Vl.


Q. What is the purpose of your direct testimony in this proceeding?

A. The purpose of my direct testimony is to describe how proposed Route Vl will negatively

affect my ranch, and to explain how the unique wildlife habitat in San Saba County will be

harmed bythe displacementcaused bythistransmission line.


Q. Was this material prepared byyou or underyour supervision


A. This has been prepared by myself; James C. Reed.



pg. 4                                    James C. Reed Irrevocable Trust - James Reed Direct Testimony
          Il. DESCRIPTION OF THE JAMES C. REED IRREVOCABLE TRUST RANCH


The ranch owned by the James C. Reed Irrevocable Trust consists of approximately 282.19

acres located in San Saba County, Texas. The property includes approximately 1,560 feet of

frontage along U.S. Highway 190. The ranch is characterized by large mesquite trees,

mature oaktrees, rolling Centra[Texas hills, dense brush cover, ponds, and substantial

native wildlife habitat. Tract #4580 & #4581




Q. What buildings or dwellings are currently on the ranch, and are there future plans

for improvements?

A. The ranch currently has no residential buildings or dwellings. It does have working cattle

pens. The property was purchased with the intention of being a future retirement

destination, and there are plans to eventually build a residence and other improvements

forthat purpose.


Q. Please describe the wildlife on the property.

A. The property supports a wide variety of wildlife species. There are multiple ponds

stocked with fish that serve as important habitat and attract ducks duringthe winter

months. The ranch is home to white-tailed deer, foxes, bobcats, coyotes, doves, and

multiple species of birds of prey. Of particular importance are the ongoing restoration

efforts for the remaining bobwhite quail population on the property and the wild turkey

population that uses the ranch for nesting duringthe spring.


pg. 5                                    James C. Reed Irrevocable Trust - James Reed Direct Testimony
 Q. How did you acquire this ranch, and why is it important to you?

A. The ranch was purchased in 2009 by my father, who later gave the propertyto me. His

goal was to leave something meaningful to his son and to create a place where future

generationsof our familycould experiencethe outdoors, enjoythe land, and appreciate the

natural beauty of the Texas landscape.




                   Ill. EFFECT OF THE PROPOSED TRANSMISSION LINE


Q. Which proposed route directly impacts your ranch?

A. Proposed Route Vl directly impacts my ranch by crossingthe upper/front portion of the

property.


Q. Please describe how the property is used today and how the proposed transmission

line may affect that use.

A. My property is used as a wildlife restoration ranch and as a place for family recreation. It

has been a place for me and my family to spend time together, hunt, fish, and enjoythe

outdoors. I have visited this ranch since childhood and have countless memories there

with family and friends. My wife harvested her first deer and shot her first hog with a bow on

this property.


The proposed Route Vl does not follow the road frontage along U.S. Highway 190, nor does

it track along an existing property boundary line. Instead, it cuts directly across the front




pg. 6                                      James C. Reed Irrevocable Trust - James Reed Direct Testimony
 quarter of my property, which is unlike many other properties along the route where the line

generally follows boundaries or road corridors.


The proposed route passes directly adjacentto the largest pond on the property. This pond

serves as a major destination for migratory waterfowl traveling south during winter months.

The line would interfere with flight paths for ducks, doves, and other bird species.


Additionally, the proposed route runs directlythrough the mostdensely populated

bobwhite quail habitat on my ranch. This area has been the focus of years of restoration

efforts. Thetransmission line would fragment habitat, increase disturbance, and likely

displacethese already declining populations.


The route also cuts across a major wildlife corridor used by deer and other game species to

move from the front portion of the ranch to the back. By crossingthrough the center of

active wildlife movement areas rather than along an existing corridor such as a roadway,

the line creates unnecessary disruption.


In myopinion, the construction and operation of this line willcause significantwildlife

displacement and may permanently damage or eliminate some of the remaining bobwhite

quail habitat in this portion of San Saba County. The impact to the natural character of the

property, as well as its future residential and recreational use, will be substantial.




pg. 7                                      James C. Reed Irrevocable Trust - James Reed Direct Testimony
                               IV. Recreation and Future Plans


Q. Do you thinkthe proposed transmission line will affect any planned future use on

your property?


A. Yes, the recreational use and enjoyment of the ranch will be changed not only for myself

but for my family forever. The plans for a retirement home will have to be altered due to the

location of the line. The wildlife restoration that has been watched and monitored will have

to change paths and figure out how to manage with the displacementthat will come with

the proposed Vl transmission line. This willdiminish notonlythe potentialthat my property

holds but also the value not only monetarily, but for my family's legacy; all for the benefit of

power companies' goals and ambitions, that have no benefit to myself or my family.


Q. How would this this transmission line affect the rural community for San Saba

County?


A. The proposed 765-kV lines proposed through San Saba County will have absolutely no

meaningful value to the community and will diminish the natural beauty and historical

character of the Heart of Texas region. Central Texas is known fortheir miles and miles of

native flowers, includingTexas Bluebonnet and the Indian Paintbrush. U.S. Highway 190 is a

popular road to travel to enjoy Texas Blue Bonnets in the spring and to soak in some of the

most breath taking sunset and sunrise views Texas has to offer. Allowingthese proposed

transmission lines to obstruct those views will not add value to the rural community, which

relies heavily on visitors travelingthrough the area to support local businesses.


pg. 8                                     James C. Reed Irrevocable Trust - James Reed Direct Testimony
                                  V. FINANCIAL DETRIMENT


Q. What are the direct financial losses foryou?


A. My ranch's value comes directly from the location and the sense of being a part of the

rural Texas landscape. Its market value relies on the scenic setting of rolling hills and

undeveloped, untouched Texas landscape. My family has invested hard-earned moneyinto

this property to make it our own piece of Texas, and to see the property devalued over

power-linesthat have no benefit to me is dishearteningto be a multi-generational Texan. I

have countless memories, money, blood, sweat, and tears poured into this property and to

see it potentially being devalued for someone else's gains is intolerable.




                                      VI. CONCLUSION


Q. Please summarize your position.

A. I appreciateyou considering mytestimony. I respectfullyoppose proposed Route Vl

because it unnecessarily crosses the interior of my ranch which has a tremendous impact

towards my ranch. The route will negatively affect the ranch's use as a wildlife restoration

property, disrupt important habitat for native and migratory species, diminish the value and

enjoyment of the property for my family, and interfere with the long-term plans to use this




pg. 9                                     James C. Reed Irrevocable Trust - James Reed Direct Testimony
 land as a retirement homestead. I askthatthe Commission reject Route Vl and select an

alternative route that avoids these impacts.
